OPENPLAN GRANTS: APPLICATION PACKET



Active Transportation
Program (ATP)
Competitive California program for walking, biking and rolling projects, plans and
non-infrastructure programs, funded from federal and state sources. Under the 2027
ATP Guidelines (Cycle 8, adopted March 19, 2026), funds are split 50 percent to the
Statewide Component, 10 percent to the Small Urban and Rural Component (areas of
5,001 to 200,000 people, and rural areas of 5,000 or less) and 40 percent to the MPO
Component; each component directs at least 25 percent to projects that benefit
disadvantaged communities.

Study place: Synthetic County, CA (county, GEOID 06998)
Applicant not entered in OpenPlan
The study place is the area recorded for the linked project in OpenPlan. It does not state the
project limits.

Appendix B. Crash summary
Source: Crash acquisition 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000701. Retrieved: Nov 20, 2026, 10:10
UTC. No content hash is stored for this record.

Source: California Crash Reporting System (CCRS)

Years requested: 2022–2025

Severity coverage: Serious-injury crashes are counted from the source's injured-person
records, joined to each crash. The crash file alone does not separate them. Classification
completeness still requires review.

Crash area: Place boundary

Crashes outside the boundary, left out: 261

Boundary counts: Complete for the boundary

Crashes reported: 80

Crashes mapped: 80

Retrieval truncated: No

Fatal crashes: 2

Serious-injury crashes: 12

Other injury crashes: 63

Property-damage-only crashes: 3

Crashes with no casualty count from the source: 0

Fatal and serious-injury crashes: 14

      Crash records are reported collisions retrieved from the source agency, not
      modeled estimates. Coverage, geocoding completeness, and severity detail vary by
      source and year. Review the coverage summary before relying on any count.
      Crashes are counted inside the place boundary. 261 crashes inside its bounding
      rectangle but outside the boundary are left out.
      Serious-injury crashes are counted from the source's injured-person records,
      joined to each crash. The crash file alone does not separate them.
      The source supplied no exact publication cutoff. The requested years and latest
      returned crash are not used as substitutes.
      This source records no person-level detail, so who was involved cannot be counted
      from it, only whether a collision was flagged as involving a pedestrian, bicyclist or
      motorcyclist.
      The safety screening score in the ATP screening packet comes from the corridor
      analysis run's own crash read. Its source and crash years print there and can differ
      from this acquisition's.
      California Crash Reporting System (CCRS): 80 crashes reported, 80 geocoded,
      years 2022–2025. Source ingest 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000701.

      12.A, by the Guidelines' names and in their order. A community qualifies by
      meeting at least one. The Guidelines state each criterion's threshold and data year.
      No row above is a determination that a community is disadvantaged or that the
      project benefits one. The applicant shows that in the application.
      The ACS proxy is a screening measure. It is not the Guidelines' median household
      income criterion or any other criterion above.
